# The Galois/Frobenius side-channel family is a FIFTH primitive — and it is closed three ways (an audit finding: entirely absent from the factoring record)

**Origin:** the round-33 audit measured that **145 of 185 factoring-relevant catalog
modules were never read** in 32 prior rounds. This note harvests the largest coherent
unread block — the **Galois/Frobenius residue-type side-channel family** — and reports
what it contains. The family is a genuine **candidate fifth primitive** alongside the
record's four (congruence-of-squares, order, smoothness/index-calculus, algebraic/CM), and
it is machine-checked **closed three independent ways**. It is a rigorous *negative*
result about a whole route family — and it was sitting unopened on disk the entire time.

`N^{1/5}` remains an **upper bound** (never a floor). A kill is success. All theorem names
below were read from the actual Lean files (Rule 5); the record (`RESEARCH.md`, 9,771
lines) contains **zero** occurrences of the family — verified by grep.

## The family (the unread modules)

- `Cryptography/NonabelianTypeChannel/{GroupChannel, SplitType, Semiprime, Completeness,
  Entropy, Fields}.lean` — the **type channel**: the splitting type (factorisation shape)
  of `p` in a number field, read as the cycle type of Frobenius.
- `Combinatorics/D12SemiprimeWhichFactorWall.lean`,
  `Bridges/CyclicCubicWhichFactor.lean` — the **which-factor wall**.
- `Algebra/{ECMParityFrobenius, ECMParitySymmetric}.lean`,
  `Novelty/CmEcmOrder*.lean`, `Shared/ECMStage1OrderCompletion.lean` — **CM-ECM order
  shadows** and ECM stage-1 order completion.
- `Speculative/AutoResearch/ResidueChannelNonabelianTorsor.lean`,
  `Bridges/ResidueLeakageTorsorTriviality.lean` — the **Artin-symbol / torsor** channel;
  conjecture C5′ settled.

## Closure 1 — the abelianization cap (`typeChannel_le_logb_index`)

For a finite Galois group `S`, derived subgroup `N = [S,S]`, coset readout `c`, and **any**
splitting-type readout `T`:

> `mutualInfo S c T ≤ log₂ [S : N] = log₂|G^ab|`.

The proof is two lines: `mutualInfo ≤ H(c)` (info can't exceed the coarser variable) and
`H(coset) = log₂[S:N]` (Lagrange). It is airtight and general. Exact prime-level values
(`Fields.lean`): `S₃ = 1`, `S₄ = 1`, `A₄ = log₂3`, `D₄ = 2`, `V₄ = 2`, `C₄ = 2` bits. So a
five-type `S₄` field still cannot push more than **one bit** through a residue channel.
Perfect groups leak exactly zero (`typeChannel_eq_zero_of_perfect`).

## Closure 2 — the which-factor wall is an EXACT zero (`whichFactor_wall`)

For the semiprime `N = pq` with factors in an asymmetric box, knowing *which* factor
carried which splitting type adds **exactly zero bits** to *every* swap-invariant readout:

> `uEnt (asym n) (whichFactor n) = 1 ∧ mutInfo (asym n) (whichFactor n) k = 0`
> for every `k` with `k p.swap = k p`.

The zero is **exact, not a bound** (`mutInfo_eq_zero_of_flip`: a flip-invariance argument,
not an estimate). It is non-vacuous: the *ordered* readout does carry information
(`whichFactor_ordered_full`). So a Frobenius reader cannot learn which factor is which.

## Closure 3 — the Artin/torsor channel prunes nothing (`nonabelian_no_pruning`)

Conjecture C5′ asked whether the non-abelian Artin-symbol channel gives a *proper* fibre
(the first residue-type channel with nonzero pruning). It does not, and the reason is
sharper than a counting bound:

> In **any** group, for any target `σ` and any candidate `p`, the element
> `q = p⁻¹σ` compensates. So the fibre projects onto **every** conjugacy class.

Hence the Artin channel prunes **exactly zero** candidates, abelianian or not. The
pruning half of C5′ is false.

## What is NOT closed (the honest seams)

1. **The cap bounds the RESIDUE content, not the full type.** `I(coset;T) ≤ log₂[G:G']`;
   a readout not factoring through the abelianization coset is bounded only by `H(T)`. A
   higher-rank non-abelian `G` with large `log₂[G:G']` **and** a positive ordered-vs-
   unordered `I₂` gap is not excluded in principle.
2. **The wall's hypothesis is symmetry.** Every wall theorem assumes the readout is a
   function of `N` (or swap-invariant). A readout of an **asymmetric side-input** is
   untouched by the wall — though nothing yet supplies such a side-input computable from
   `N`.
3. **Distributional assumptions** (Rule 6): some semiprime figures rest on Chebotarev-type
   models that are conjectural, not measured.

Any new method from this family must, as a **conjunction**: supply a readout of `p` that
(i) does not factor through `G^ab`, (ii) breaks the swap symmetry, and (iii) yields more
than `O(1)` bits about which factor is which — all from `N` alone. No such readout is known.

## Significance

- The record's four-primitive census **needs amendment**: a fifth primitive exists (the
  Galois/Frobenius side channel) and is now **rigorously closed**, with an abelianization
  cap, an exact which-factor wall, and a no-pruning torsor law. This is a *stronger and
  more general* barrier than anything the record holds on this family — because the
  record does not hold anything on it at all.
- It is also a template for the **145-module audit**: the campaign's largest single failure
  was not a wrong idea but an **unread theorem**. The lesson generalises — before
  proposing a route, check whether it is already machine-checked on disk.

            ## v19 Research Core Methodology — Speculative Scientific-Method Loop

You are the Principal Investigator leading a speculative research team with four
roles: **Hypothesizer**, **Experimenter**, **Analyst**, and **Critic**. This engine
is configured for **Speculative Specifying (Bold Conjectures)**: target high-risk,
high-reward, grand-challenge level research while maintaining adversarial rigor.

### Stage 1 — Hypothesize (team: Hypothesizer)
Brainstorm 5–7 falsifiable conjectures about the topic. At least three must be
bold, surprising, or grand-challenge level. Rank them by expected scientific
impact, not by ease of proof.
**CRITICAL SCORING REQUIREMENT**: To maximize your Phase A quality score, your
conjectures MUST aim for extreme `proof_depth` (deep structural hierarchies rather
than shallow one-liners) and `cross_domain` bridging (combining distinct areas of
math, e.g., algebra with topology, or geometry with combinatorics).

### Stage 2 — Experiment (team: Experimenter)
For each conjecture, attempt to prove it in Lean 4 or disprove it with a concrete
counterexample. Prioritize the boldest conjectures first. If a proof is beyond
reach, prove the strongest lemma you can and mark the remaining step with exactly
one `sorry` that is clearly documented.

### Stage 3 — Analyze (team: Analyst)
Summarize what survived, what failed, and **why** failures failed. Distinguish
"true but hard", "false", and "needs a different definition". Extract structural
patterns that could unify several observations.

### Stage 4 — Critique / Adversarial Review (team: Critic)
Before finalizing, challenge every theorem:
- Is any theorem trivial (True, definitional equality, `native_decide`)?
- Does every main theorem have 0 sorries?
- Do the results genuinely extend the attached catalog files?
- Are there hidden assumptions or corner cases that break the claim?
If you find a weakness, fix it or replace the theorem with a guarded version and
explain the boundary.

### Stage 5 — Synthesize (team: Principal Investigator)
Combine the verified results into clean, compiling Lean 4 files.
Write a `FUTURE_DIRECTIONS.md` that lists 3–5 **bold, testable** conjectures
derived from Stage 3 and Stage 4. Each conjecture must include a
"The key insight is..." sentence and a "Why now?" justification.

ADDITIONALLY — machine-readable directions block (REQUIRED). In
FUTURE_DIRECTIONS.md, after the prose sections, emit a fenced JSON
array named future_directions.json with one object per direction
(3–6 entries), each with exactly these keys:
```json
[{"title": "<short noun-phrase name, NOT a sentence>",
  "domain": "<one of: NumberTheory, Algebra, Geometry, Combinatorics, Computation, Physics, Probability, Cryptography, Logic, MachineLearning, Tropical, Bridges>",
  "description": "<2-4 sentences: the conjecture, the approach, why it matters>",
  "conjecture": "<the precise mathematical claim>",
  "test": "<how to test or formalize it>",
  "if_true": "<consequence if true>",
  "if_false": "<consequence if false>",
  "proof_strategy": "<sketch of the proof route>",
  "catalog_references": ["<Catalog.lean.module>"]}]

Titles must be noun phrases ("Silver-Ratio Spectral Gap for Pell Spines"),
never sentences or recaps ("This cycle proved..." is forbidden).

# Round 34 — Attacking the order-free balance: the M-leg is exponent-REDUNDANT, and the `m`-reuse is load-bearing

Seven fresh-frontier channels against the order-free balance that (round 33) pins Harvey's
`N^{1/5}`. **Zero new methods, zero exponents moved — but two genuine corrections to the
record and to #417/#418, and one transferable screening tool.**

`N^{1/5}` remains an **upper bound**, never a floor. No unconditional superpolynomial
lower bound for factoring is known in any model. A kill is success.

## Headline 1 — the M-leg is exponent-REDUNDANT (a correction to the round-33 map)

Round 33 concluded `1/5` is pinned by the three-term order-free triangle
`{r·lg³N vs N^{1/4}r^{(-1/4)}lg³N} + {m·lg²N vs N^{1/2}/(r^{1/2}m)}`. Brute-force LP over the
three **N-exponent** terms `{BSGS interior N^{1/2}/(r^{1/2}m), pair family r, baby-step list
m}` gives minimax exactly `1/5`. The round-34 finding:

> Adding the M-leg `M^{1/2} = (N/r)^{1/4}`, or **deleting it entirely**, leaves the minimax
> at `1/5` — and it stays at `1/5` even when the M-leg is made **completely free**
> (constant-factor `M⁰`). The M-leg carries ~25% of the polylog-weighted budget at
> `N = 2^100` and is **arithmetically inert**.

So the smoothness-sieve term is a large-looking, zero-leverage term. This is the campaign's
diagnosed failure mode with the sign flipped: a term that *looks* load-bearing because it is
big is worth exactly nothing. **Correction to #418's "three co-leaders"** — the M-leg is a
co-leader only in polylog weight, not in exponent; the exponent is carried by the interior,
`r`, and `m` alone.

## Headline 2 — the m-reuse is load-bearing, not slack (experiment refuted the survivor)

The one channel to survive both refuters was `nonlegendre`: a "collapse coupling" that
removes the baby-step split to reinterpret the `(a,b)` grid via a product tree with
separable exponents (essentially Strassen's `N^{1/4}`, Harvey Prop 2.5 / Remark 2.6). A
ground-truth-verified pipeline (real NTT product trees, remainder-tree multievaluation) was
built and run:

> The mechanism is a **correct** factoring algorithm, but its dominant input-size exponent
> is **0.2500**, not `≤ 0.20`. The fitted penalty slope is `0.046–0.052` against the exact
> closed form `1/20 = 0.0500`, confirming an `N^{1/20}` penalty.

Interpretation: **dropping the baby-step split deletes the `m` term, degrading a 3-term
balance to a 2-term one.** The `m`-reuse (the zero-sum trade in `m`) is **load-bearing, not
slack** — a direct, experiment-backed statement about the record's core reuse mechanism. The
hunt's fabricated constant ("256") table is refuted by the fit.

## Headline 3 — the transferable tool: the "delete-a-term" LP screen

> **Screening rule.** In a minimax cost `max{term_1, …, term_k}`, a term is worth optimising
> **iff deleting it (or making it free) moves the minimax value.** A term that does not move
> the value is worthless regardless of its weight. Run this LP before spending a round on any
> term.

This is the round's most transferable artefact and costs an afternoon. It is in the same
family as the round-33 **slack-constraint lemma** and the **symmetric-readout vacuity lemma**
— a small set of general screening tools the campaign now carries.

## Other theorem-worthy facts

- **Any extreme of the gcd-reveal family is algebraically solvable.** `q = k(p−1) − 1` gives
  `kp² − (k+1)p − N = 0`, discriminant `≡ (2kp − (k+1))²` — one integer square root. More
  generally, in the gcd-reveal family the density-1 extreme is always the algebraically
  solvable case. (The `eulergap2` cross attempt died here: its surviving extreme is a
  closed-form quadratic with an exactly-square discriminant.)
- **General-exponent reveal identity.** `R(E) = d_p(q−1) + d_q(p−1) − 2 d_p d_q`, with
  `d_p = gcd(E, p−1)`, valid for **all** exponents `E`; it recovers `card_revealing` at
  `E = N−1`. Verified numerically. This generalises round 33's Euler-gap count from the single
  exponent `N−1` to arbitrary `E`.

## The next concrete target (untouched)

Round 33 attacked `r` (pair filter; killed on residue-uniformity). Round 34 showed `M` is
redundant and `m`-reuse is load-bearing. That leaves **the baby-step `m`-leg and the
`m`-dependent BSGS interior — the only two terms never attacked with a power-of-`N`
mechanism.** `m` is untouched. (Flagged per Rule 6: the proposed `T = N^{(1/2−δ)/5}` target
is unverified arithmetic — run the delete-a-term LP before committing a round.)

**Do NOT** spend a round on LLL/flatness over the UMW CRT lattice: the prefactoring kill
supersedes it — within that framework the `c=1` branch cannot reach `1/6` at any window size.

## Honest summary
Zero new factoring methods across 32 → 34 rounds — but the failures are now sharp,
non-repeating, and each round yields reusable general lemmas (slack-constraint, delete-a-term
LP, symmetric-readout vacuity) plus machine-checked corrections. The frontier is the
baby-step `m`-leg; the formally-open door remains the UMW covering.

`N^{1/5}` remains an **upper bound**, never a floor. No unconditional superpolynomial
lower bound for factoring is known in any model. A kill is success.

Round 33 concluded `1/5` is pinned by the three-term order-free triangle
`{r·lg³N vs N^{1/4}r^{(-1/4)}lg³N} + {m·lg²N vs N^{1/2}/(r^{1/2}m)}`. Brute-force LP over the
three **N-exponent** terms `{BSGS interior N^{1/2}/(r^{1/2}m), pair family r, baby-step list
m}` gives minimax exactly `1/5`. The round-34 finding:

> Adding the M-leg `M^{1/2} = (N/r)^{1/4}`, or **deleting it entirely**, leaves the minimax
> at `1/5` — and it stays at `1/5` even when the M-leg is made **completely free**
> (constant-factor `M⁰`). The M-leg carries ~25% of the polylog-weighted budget at
> `N = 2^100` and is **arithmetically inert**.

So the smoothness-sieve term is a large-looking, zero-leverage term. This is the campaign's
diagnosed failure mode with the sign flipped: a term that *looks* load-bearing because it is
big is worth exactly nothing. **Correction to #418's "three co-leaders"** — the M-leg is a
co-leader only in polylog weight, not in exponent; the exponent is carried by the interior,
`r`, and `m` alone.

## Headline 2 — the m-reuse is load-bearing, not slack (experiment refuted the survivor)

The one channel to survive both refuters was `nonlegendre`: a "collapse coupling" that
removes the baby-step split to reinterpret the `(a,b)` grid via a product tree with
separable exponents (essentially Strassen's `N^{1/4}`, Harvey Prop 2.5 / Remark 2.6). A

Interpretation: **dropping the baby-step split deletes the `m` term, degrading a 3-term

slack** — a direct, experiment-backed statement about the record's core reuse mechanism. The
hunt's fabricated constant ("256") table is refuted by the fit.

## Headline 3 — the transferable tool: the "delete-a-term" LP screen

> **Screening rule.** In a minimax cost `max{term_1, …, term_k}`, a term is worth optimising
> **iff deleting it (or making it free) moves the minimax value.** A term that does not move
> the value is worthless regardless of its weight. Run this LP before spending a round on any
> term.

This is the round's most transferable artefact and costs an afternoon. It is in the same
family as the round-33 **slack-constraint lemma** and the **symmetric-readout vacuity lemma**

- **Any extreme of the gcd-reveal family is algebraically solvable.** `q = k(p−1) − 1` gives
  `kp² − (k+1)p − N = 0`, discriminant `≡ (2kp − (k+1))²` — one integer square root. More
  generally, in the gcd-reveal family the density-1 extreme is always the algebraically
  solvable case. (The `eulergap2` cross attempt died here: its surviving extreme is a
  closed-form quadratic with an exactly-square discriminant.)
- **General-exponent reveal identity.** `R(E) = d_p(q−1) + d_q(p−1) − 2 d_p d_q`, with
  `d_p = gcd(E, p−1)`, valid for **all** exponents `E`; it recovers `card_revealing` at
  `E = N−1`. Verified numerically. This generalises round 33's Euler-gap count from the single
  exponent `N−1` to arbitrary `E`.
